overview.text: The Annunciation depicts Gabriel’s announcement to Mary in Nazareth that she will bear Jesus. Hopko’s explanation places the feast on March 25, nine months before the Nativity, and identifies Luke 1:26–38 as the biblical account.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening paragraph and quoted Gospel passage

blocks.text: Gabriel approaches Mary, who may sit or stand near a throne-like seat. Some compositions show her spinning; the messenger carries a staff or scroll.

blocks.text: The account includes Gabriel’s greeting, Mary’s question, the announcement of the Holy Spirit’s action, and her assent. Hopko notes that the feast’s Matins canon takes the form of dialogue between Gabriel and Mary. He describes the date’s frequent occurrence within Great Lent and the resulting variations in its services. The calendar placement concerns the Church’s celebration, while the icon’s subject is the Gospel encounter itself.
